lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Describe three different organiser ideas for Jordan in words, as if you were labelling quick sketches. Each idea must change the shape or how the pencils are held, and name one criterion it tries to meet. Do not offer the same tray in three colours.

FEEDBACK
Three ideas should differ in structure, such as a flat tray, a long sleeve and a standing holder. Each note says how the eight pencils sit and which check it targets: holding 8, fitting the 15 cm corner, or keeping edges smooth. A pencil Jordan measured at 18 cm will stick out of a 15 cm corner if it lies flat, so a flat idea must admit that limit. Three sticker colours of one box are still one idea.

WATCH FOR
Calling three sticker colours of the same box three ideas, when the pencil-holding structure never changes. Colour is decoration. Variety means a different shape or a different way of holding the pencils. Replace the colour list with three structures that do different jobs against the criteria.

WORKED MODEL
Three word-sketches differ in structure: a flat corner tray, an 18 cm sleeve, and a standing roll.
